Lena R: Heads-up 1 an IC is asking about bumping to L5. Manager wants effective date 2026-05-01. What's the latest submit date for promo packet and payroll? @Arjun (People Ops)
Arjun (People Ops): Hi @Lena R 1 to guarantee payroll on 2026-05-01 get the packet in by 2026-04-18 EOD PT. We need manager rec, updated role profile, evidence links, and proposed comp. Payroll runs the night before the effective date.
Lena R: If we miss that, can we still apply retro to May 1, or is it only forward?
Maya (People Ops): If approval happens after the payroll cutoff we can apply retro pay back to the requested effective date, but processing timing depends on when approvals land. If retro is >60 days, finance must approve separately.
Jorge (Finance): Confirming Maya. Retro >60 days requires a finance review and will likely land in the next payroll cycle after approval. Also tag the payroll row with code "PROMO-RETRO" so we process properly.
Lena R: OK. Manager also asked about using a one-time market adjustment vs base increase because candidate sits at top of band. Can we do a small market adjust + equity refresh instead?
Arjun (People Ops): Yes. Options are: 1) base increase (if within budget and band) 2) one-time market adjustment (taxed as bonus) 3) equity refresh (requires grants team sign-off). For market adjust use payroll code "COMP-ADJ". For equity, include expected grant size in packet so compensation committee sees total comp impact.
Lena R: For IC->manager conversions, any extra docs? Manager asked about leadership calibration.
Maya (People Ops): IC->manager requires a leadership calibration queue and a 2-up sign-off. Add direct reports list and scope doc. Expect an extra ~7 business days for review. If you need a tight effective date, push packet earlier.
Lena R: What about promotions tied to hire-time negotiation (pre-offer higher comp)?
Arjun (People Ops): Include the offer email thread and mark packet "pre-negotiated-comp". Those go to exec comp committee during calibration.
Jorge (Finance): FYI also include cost-center and budget owner approval. If the bump increases OTE beyond budget, the budget owner must sign and we may convert to a phased increase.
Lena R: Any tax implications on retro pay the manager should warn the employee about?
Jorge (Finance): Retro pay is taxed in the pay period it hits, so employees may see higher withholding that period. Recommend managers mention this. For large retros, offer to model net-pay impact via payroll.
comp-bot: Packet created for candidate by Lena R 1 status: metadata recorded. Auto-scheduled calibration window: 2026-04-20 to 2026-04-22.
Lena R: Perfect 1 thanks all — I'll submit by EOD 2026-04-16 to be safe.
